instagram_reel.script:
Fall Into Spice is back, and this dinner is doing something really special. On Saturday, November 21, two kitchens are cooking together at The Depanneur in Toronto.

Noir X is bringing Caribbean flavours. Vit Béo is bringing Vietnamese-inspired dishes with a Toronto twist. And I’m pairing wine to every course.

We’ve got a welcome sparkling pour, four courses, two palate cleansers, and wine with each dish. The menu moves from Chinese doughnut and pho-spiced beef tartare, to macaroni pie, to stew chicken, and ends with soursop gâteau basque.

This is the kind of dinner that makes people talk to each other. Come hungry.

linkedin.post:
Fall Into Spice is back for a second event in the 2026 series, and this dinner is a great example of what happens when food and wine are allowed to meet on equal footing.

On Saturday, November 21, Noir X and Vit Béo are cooking together at The Depanneur in Toronto. The menu brings Caribbean and Vietnamese-inspired flavours to the same table, with fresh herbs, citrus, aromatics and heat running through the meal.

Those flavour profiles make for a rewarding wine pairing experience, even though they’re still too often left out of wine conversation. That’s the work I love most: building a dinner where the pairing is thoughtful, the food leads, and the wines support the whole story.

The format includes a welcome sparkling pour, four courses, two palate cleansers, and a wine pairing with every course. It’s the kind of event that creates real conversation between chefs, guests, and the glasses in front of them.

If you’re interested in food-forward hospitality, cross-cultural collaboration, or wine programming that feels more inclusive and more current, this is one to watch.

quote_card: The food leads, and the wines have to keep up.
